    def observe_solution(
    times: Sequence[float] | np.ndarray,
    trajectory: Array,
    observations: Sequence[ObservationSpec],
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, object] | None = None,
) -> ObservationResult:
    """Evaluate native named outputs at every supplied stored output time.

    Time is a static, finite, strictly increasing host grid. Each callback must
    return an array in the trajectory namespace and dtype with its declared
    shape. Native values are stacked without conversion or gradient detachment.
    Inputs and returned arrays should be treated as immutable.

    Args:
        times: Stored output times, independent of internal solver step times.
        trajectory: Native state history with a leading output-time dimension.
        observations: Unique named evaluators with static output metadata.
        params: Parameters passed to each evaluator, including observation-only ones.

    Returns:
        Native series and evaluation coverage. No interpolation/error estimate.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If grids, trajectory shape, metadata or output shapes disagree.
        TypeError: If states/outputs violate the real floating native-array contract.
    """
    grid = np.asarray(times)
    if (
        grid.ndim != 1
        or grid.size == 0
        or grid.dtype.kind not in "fiu"
        or not np.all(np.isfinite(grid))
        or not np.all(grid[1:] > grid[:-1])
    ):
        msg = "observation times must be a nonempty finite strictly increasing 1D grid"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    if not trajectory.shape or trajectory.shape[0] != grid.size:
        msg = "trajectory must have one leading state row per observation time"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    xp = array_namespace(trajectory)
    if not xp.isdtype(trajectory.dtype, "real floating"):
        msg = "observation trajectory must have a real floating dtype"
        raise TypeError(msg)
    _validate_specs(observations)
    static_times = tuple(float(time) for time in grid)
    states = cast("_Indexable", trajectory)
    series = {}
    for spec in observations:
        values = []
        for index, time in enumerate(static_times):
            value = spec.eval_fn(
                time, states[index], **({} if params is None else params)
            )
            if (
                array_namespace(value) is not xp
                or getattr(value, "dtype", None) != trajectory.dtype
            ):
                msg = (
                    f"observation {spec.name!r} must preserve trajectory "
                    "namespace and dtype"
                )
                raise TypeError(msg)
            if getattr(value, "shape", None) != spec.metadata.output_shape:
                msg = (
                    f"observation {spec.name!r} must have shape "
                    f"{spec.metadata.output_shape}"
                )
                raise ValueError(msg)
            values.append(value)
        series[spec.name] = ObservationSeries(
            spec, cast("Array", xp.stack(values, axis=0))
        )
    return ObservationResult(
        static_times,
        MappingProxyType(series),
        ObservationDiagnostics(len(observations) * len(static_times)),
    )

    def reduce_observations(
    samples: Iterable[tuple[float, Array]],
    observations: Sequence[ObservationSpec],
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, object] | None = None,
) -> ObservationSummary:
    """Reduce a finite native sample stream in one pass without storing a trajectory.

    Samples define the exact window endpoints. Native initial/final values,
    changes and composite-trapezoid integrals preserve evaluator shapes and
    gradients. A single sample has zero duration, change and integral. Callback
    outputs are snapshotted so a producer may reuse its numerical state buffer.

    The reducer retains a constant number of output arrays and one current
    state reference. Producer storage and reverse-mode computation graphs are
    separate: no constant-memory gradient guarantee is implied. There is no
    persistent checkpoint or partial-result recovery; an interrupted call must
    restart from a producer-owned replay/checkpoint. Callbacks must be pure.

    Args:
        samples: Finite, nonempty iterable of static times and native states.
            Times must increase strictly; state shape, namespace and real floating
            dtype stay fixed. Only the supplied times define quadrature samples.
        observations: Unique named evaluators and scientific output metadata.
        params: Observation parameters passed to every callback.

    Returns:
        Bounded-size native reductions with window, sample count and diagnostics.
        Integrals inherit trajectory and sampled-quadrature error; no dense-output
        order, event reconstruction or separate error estimate is asserted.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the stream is empty, intervals are invalid or shapes change.
        TypeError: If states or outputs violate the native namespace/dtype contract.
    """
    selection = tuple(observations)
    iterator = iter(samples)
    try:
        time, state = next(iterator)
    except StopIteration as error:
        msg = "observation summary requires at least one sample"
        raise ValueError(msg) from error
    first = _sample(_static_time(time), state, selection, params)
    layout = _StateLayout(state.shape, state.dtype, array_namespace(state))
    values = _initial_values(first)
    last_time = first.times[0]
    count = 1
    for sample_time, state in iterator:
        time = _static_time(sample_time)
        duration = time - last_time
        if not np.isfinite(duration) or duration <= 0:
            msg = "summary sample times must increase with finite intervals"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        if state.shape != layout.shape:
            msg = "summary samples must preserve state shape"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        if (
            state.dtype != layout.dtype
            or array_namespace(state) is not layout.namespace
        ):
            msg = "summary samples must preserve state namespace and dtype"
            raise TypeError(msg)
        current = _sample(time, state, selection, params)
        values = _advance_values(values, current, duration)
        last_time = time
        count += 1
    return ObservationSummary(
        (first.times[0], last_time),
        count,
        MappingProxyType(values),
        ObservationDiagnostics(count * len(selection)),
    )

    def register_sparse_adapter(adapter: SparseAdapter, *, replace: bool = False) -> None:
    """Register an operator adapter in the existing sparse dispatch registry.

    Replacement clears that ecosystem's cached factors. Predicates must be
    pure; overlapping pair matches are rejected when dispatching a solve.

    Raises:

    if adapter.ecosystem_id in _SPARSE_ADAPTERS and not replace:

        raise ValueError(msg)
    _clear_adapter_cache(adapter.ecosystem_id)

    def sink_states(
    rhs: SteadyStateRhs,
    states: Sequence[Array],
    *,
    t: float = 0.0,
    jacobian: SteadyStateJacobian | None = None,
    tol: float = 1e-9,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return a mask of states no derivative depends on.

    Cumulative counters and absorbing compartments that feed nothing back have
    a zero Jacobian column. They never reach a zero derivative while their
    inflow is positive, so hold them fixed in :func:`steady_state`.

    Args:
        rhs: ``rhs(t, y) -> dy/dt``.
        states: Sample states.
        t: Evaluation time.
        jacobian: Dense Jacobian callback; central differences by default.
        tol: Largest column entry, relative to the largest Jacobian entry,
            still treated as zero.

    Returns:
        Boolean ``(n_state,)`` mask.
    """
    jacobian = jacobian or _central_difference_jacobian(rhs)
    columns = np.zeros(0)
    for y in states:
        magnitude = np.abs(np.asarray(jacobian(t, y), dtype=np.float64)).max(axis=0)
        columns = magnitude if columns.size == 0 else np.maximum(columns, magnitude)
    return columns <= tol * max(float(columns.max(initial=0.0)), 1e-300)

    def smooth(
    x: NDArray[np.floating],
    alpha: float = 0.02,
    out: NDArray[np.floating] | None = None,
) -> NDArray[np.floating]:
    """
    Apply simple smoothing along the last axis.

    Args:
        x: Input array to smooth.
        alpha: Smoothing factor between 0 and 1.
        out: Optional output array to store the result.

    Returns:
        Smoothed array with the same shape as x.
    """
    x_arr = np.asarray(x)
    smoothed = (1.0 - alpha) * x_arr + alpha * x_arr.mean(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    if out is not None:
        np.copyto(out, smoothed)
        return out
    return cast("NDArray[np.floating]", smoothed)

    def solve_linear(
    request: LinearSolveRequest, solver: LinearSolver
) -> LinearSolveResult:
    """Call an eager solver and verify every original, unpreconditioned residual.

    Returns:
        Candidate solution and per-column diagnostics, including failures.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If namespace, dtype or callback metadata is invalid.
        ValueError: If operator/RHS/result dimensions or iteration counts disagree.
    """
    rhs = request.rhs
    if not isinstance(rhs, np.ndarray) or rhs.dtype not in (np.float32, np.float64):  # noqa: PLR6201 - dtype equality is not hash equality
        msg = "checked linear solves require eager NumPy float32/float64 RHS arrays"
        raise TypeError(msg)
    shape = request.operator.shape
    if request.operator.dtype != rhs.dtype or (
        isinstance(request.operator, ActionOperator)
        and request.operator.namespace is not array_namespace(rhs)
    ):
        msg = "operator must match the NumPy RHS dtype and namespace"
        raise TypeError(msg)
    if len(shape) != 2 or shape[0] != shape[1] or len(rhs.shape) not in {1, 2}:
        msg = "checked linear solves require a square operator and vector/matrix RHS"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    if shape[0] != rhs.shape[0]:
        msg = "operator and RHS dimensions disagree"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    preconditioner = request.preconditioner
    if preconditioner is not None and (
        preconditioner.shape != shape
        or preconditioner.dtype != rhs.dtype
        or preconditioner.namespace is not array_namespace(rhs)
    ):
        msg = "inverse preconditioner must match operator shape and RHS dtype/namespace"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    candidate = solver(request)
    _numpy_like(candidate.value, rhs, "solve result")
    if not isinstance(candidate.success, bool):
        msg = "solver success must be a Python bool"
        raise TypeError(msg)
    if (
        not isinstance(candidate.iterations, Integral)
        or isinstance(candidate.iterations, bool)
        or not 0 <= candidate.iterations <= request.options.max_iterations
    ):
        msg = "solver iterations must be an integer within the requested budget"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    product = request.operator @ candidate.value
    _numpy_like(product, rhs, "operator result")
    # Accumulate float32 norms in float64 to avoid avoidable sum-of-squares overflow.
    residual = rhs.astype(np.float64) - cast("np.ndarray", product).astype(np.float64)
    residual_norm = np.atleast_1d(np.hypot.reduce(np.abs(residual), axis=0))
    rhs_norm = np.atleast_1d(np.hypot.reduce(np.abs(rhs.astype(np.float64)), axis=0))
    tolerance = np.maximum(request.options.atol, request.options.rtol * rhs_norm)
    converged = (
        np.isfinite(residual_norm)
        & np.isfinite(rhs_norm)
        & (residual_norm <= tolerance)
        & np.atleast_1d(np.all(np.isfinite(candidate.value), axis=0))
        & candidate.success
    )
    diagnostics = LinearSolveDiagnostics(
        converged, residual_norm, tolerance, candidate.iterations, candidate.message
    )
    return LinearSolveResult(candidate.value, diagnostics)

    def solve_sensitivities(
    system: SensitivitySystem,
    parameters: Mapping[str, object],
    initial: SensitivityInitial,
    time_grid: NDArray[np.floating],
    *,
    options: SensitivityOptions | None = None,
) -> SensitivitySolution:
    """Integrate ``S' = (df/dy) S + df/dtheta`` with existing explicit kernels.

    The compiler is optional: any correctly ordered derivative artifact can
    satisfy the protocol. Callbacks/mesh are static under JIT; native scalar
    bindings and both initial arrays retain their graphs. Batch independent
    systems through native vmap. Forcing jumps, events, history dependence,
    stochastic paths and operator solvers need separately qualified methods.

    Returns:
        Native retained outputs and measured sensitivities in physical coordinates.

    Raises:
        ValueError: Layout, mesh or declared storage limits disagree.
    """
    opts = options or SensitivityOptions()
    bindings = _validate_inputs(system, parameters, initial)
    xp = array_namespace(initial.state)
    n, p, m = (
        len(system.derivatives.state_names),
        len(system.parameter_names),
        len(system.derivatives.observable_names),
    )
    grid = np.asarray(time_grid, dtype=np.float64)
    if (
        grid.ndim != 1
        or not grid.size
        or not np.all(np.isfinite(grid))
        or np.any(np.diff(grid) <= 0)
    ):
        msg = "Sensitivity mesh must be finite and strictly increasing"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    count = grid.size if opts.store_history else 1
    dimension = n * (1 + p)
    if (
        dimension > opts.max_augmented_states
        or count * (n + n * p + m * p) * (xp.finfo(initial.state.dtype).bits // 8)
        > opts.max_output_bytes
    ):
        msg = "Sensitivity solve exceeds its augmented/output storage limit"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    core = ModelCore(
        dimension,
        1,
        grid,
        options=ModelCoreOptions(
            dtype=np.dtype(str(initial.state.dtype).removeprefix("torch.")),
            store_history=opts.store_history,
        ),
    )
    core.set_initial_state(
        xp.reshape(
            xp.concat((
                initial.state,
                xp.reshape(initial.parameter_derivatives, (-1,)),
            )),
            (-1, 1),
        )
    )
    CoreSolver(core).run(_augmented_rhs(system, bindings), config=opts.solver)
    return _solution(system, bindings, core, opts)

    def unregister_sparse_adapter(ecosystem_id: str) -> None:
    """Remove an adapter and release all of its cached factors.

    Raises:
        KeyError: If the adapter is not registered.
    """  # noqa: DOC502 - dictionary removal raises KeyError
    del _SPARSE_ADAPTERS[ecosystem_id]
    _clear_adapter_cache(ecosystem_id)
